title: Cost Optimization Pillar: Spend Less, Get More 💡
description: Practical techniques to reduce your AWS bill without compromising performance – the FinOps mindset.

slides.title: Cost Optimization is a Continuous Process 🔁
slides.content:
# It's Not a One‑Time Fix

Cost optimization is one of the six pillars of the AWS Well‑Architected Framework. It involves:
- Understanding and controlling where money is being spent.
- Selecting the most appropriate and right‑sized resources.
- Analysing spending over time and scaling to meet needs without overspending.

**Mindset**: It's not about being cheap; it's about maximising business value from every dollar.

slides.title: Right‑Sizing: Match Resources to Workloads 📏
slides.content:
# Don't Over‑Provision

Many organisations run instances at low utilisation (e.g., 10% CPU). Right‑sizing means selecting the optimal instance type and size for your workload.

Tools:
- **AWS Cost Explorer Rightsizing Recommendations** – identifies idle and under‑utilised EC2 instances.
- **AWS Compute Optimizer** – uses ML to recommend optimal instance types based on CPU, memory, network.
- **AWS Trusted Advisor** – flags under‑utilised EBS volumes, idle load balancers.

After identifying, stop, resize, or migrate to a smaller instance type or a different family (e.g., from m5 to t3 if bursting).

quizData.question: Which AWS service uses machine learning to recommend optimal EC2 instance types for your workloads?
quizData.explanation: Compute Optimizer analyses configuration and utilisation metrics to provide rightsizing recommendations.

slides.title: Leverage Reserved & Savings Plans 📅
slides.content:
# Commit for Long‑Term Savings

We covered the models earlier. For cost optimization:
- Review your On‑Demand usage in Cost Explorer.
- Purchase **Savings Plans** for the consistent baseline. AWS provides **recommendations** based on your past usage.
- For RIs, consider **Convertible RIs** if you expect technology changes.
- Regularly review RI/SP **utilisation reports** – if a reservation isn't being used, modify or exchange it (if convertible).

slides.title: Storage Lifecycle Management 🗄️
slides.content:
# Move Data to Cheaper Tiers

S3 Lifecycle policies (Chapter 5) are a massive cost lever. Automatically transition objects from Standard → Standard‑IA → Glacier → Deep Archive. Also:
- **Delete old EBS snapshots** and AMIs.
- **Use EFS Infrequent Access** lifecycle to move files not accessed after 30 days to a cheaper tier.
- **Enable S3 Intelligent‑Tiering** to automatically move objects without manual rules.

Storage costs often creep up because people forget to delete old data.

slides.title: Auto Scaling: Match Capacity to Demand ⚖️
slides.content:
# Don't Pay for Idle

- **EC2 Auto Scaling**: scale in during low traffic periods (e.g., evenings, weekends). Use scheduled scaling for predictable patterns.
- **Aurora Serverless / DynamoDB On‑Demand**: scale to zero when not in use.
- **Application Auto Scaling**: applies to many services (ECS, DynamoDB, Lambda provisioned concurrency).

Set minimum and desired capacity appropriately. Monitor and tune scaling policies to avoid premature scaling.

slides.title: Clean Up Unused Resources 🧹
slides.content:
# The Cost of 'Zombie' Infrastructure

- **Orphaned Elastic IPs** – charge per hour when not attached.
- **Unattached EBS volumes** – still incur storage cost.
- **Idle Load Balancers** – ALB/NLB charge per hour even with no targets.
- **Old RDS snapshots** – accumulate over time.
- **Stopped instances** – no compute charge, but EBS volumes still cost.

Schedule a regular (monthly) cleanup using scripts or AWS Config rules to detect unused resources.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Enable AWS Organizations SCPs to Restrict Expensive Services 🚫
slides.content:
## Prevent Unintentional Spend

Use Service Control Policies to deny access to expensive services or instance types in non‑production accounts. For example, deny launching `*.16xlarge` instances or deny Redshift in dev accounts. This is a hard guardrail that prevents accidental or malicious overspend.
